definitions.K: number of moments m_1..m_K the classical model must reproduce, on top of unit mass
definitions.rho_relaxed: supremum over n-term exponential sums with nonnegative density matching the moments. Every order-n phase-type density is such a sum, so this is an UPPER bound on the classical supremum. The search maximises it, so an incomplete search UNDER-reports and the figure is only a lower estimate of the true bound.
definitions.rho_direct: supremum over genuine Coxian(n) models, located by multistart. A LOWER bound on the classical supremum. Never usable as the bound itself, but it must not exceed rho_relaxed -- if it does, the relaxed search has not converged.
definitions.certifies: rho_relaxed < rho_quantum, i.e. no order-n classical renewal process matching the moments can reach the observed Fisher ratio

weight_counting: n weights against 1+K linear constraints. K = n-1 is square and leaves the freedom that makes the relaxation loose; K = n is over-determined by one, collapsing the feasible pole sets onto a variety and tightening the bound; K = n+1 can empty the class outright, at which point the moments alone falsify order n and the Fisher ratio does no work.

rows.note: the moment-matched APH2 set is exactly one-parameter and was scanned in full; rho is maximal at the pure hypoexponential endpoint, confirming the endpoint-maximizer proposition the frozen module assumes

relaxed bound exceeds rho_quantum, so order 3 is NOT certified at K=2. The maximizer has near-coincident poles and a density grazing zero -- outside the phase-type class proper -- and the relaxation is about 4x looser than the direct search.

rho_direct exceeds the relaxed figure, so the relaxed search is NOT converged and the true upper bound is at least 28.2876. The verdict is unaffected -- both sit far below rho_quantum -- and the near-equality shows the relaxation is close to tight here, unlike at K=2.
no order-3 pole set with a nonnegative density survives five constraints on three weights. The moments alone falsify order 3, so the Fisher ratio does no work at this K.
four weights against four constraints is square again, and the freedom that made K=2 loose at order 3 returns.
under-determined weights; the relaxation carries no useful information here.

conclusion.rule: matching K moments certifies that classical order K cannot reproduce the record; certifying a higher order requires a correspondingly higher moment.
conclusion.certified_statement: with (m1, m2, m3) matched, no order-3 classical renewal process reaches the observed finite-resolution Fisher ratio, by a factor of 5.5
conclusion.caveat: rho_relaxed is obtained by maximising an upper-bound functional, so every figure here is a lower estimate of the true bound and none is a proof. Only the n=2 row is exhaustive. The K=3 row is known to be under-converged, detected by the direct search exceeding it.

not_supported.reason: the O'Cinneide cone bound gives the order needed to reproduce the waiting-time density exactly (62.8 at gamma_phi = 0, 31.4 at 0.1, 15.7 at 0.3). A witness constrained only by a few moments and one Fisher ratio certifies far less; the order it reaches is set by how many moments are matched, and is single-digit here.

provenance.driver: numerics/order_scan.py regenerates this scan with its own budget; the figures above come from targeted runs with n_random 600-3000, n_refine 8-30, seeds 5 and 11
